title: finding(app-shell): Studio's Interfaces pillar crashes its nav rail when a nav item's label is a locale map ("Objects are not valid as a React child")
body:
Filing-gate category: ① a product defect with a named site, class (a). `reach:` a public door, measured: the Studio Interfaces pillar on an app whose navigation carries a spec-valid `I18nLabel` map.
- **Measured.** The objectui#11148 dev ran an uncommitted probe (deleted after, tree clean) that mounted the real `InterfacesPillar` with a mocked metadata client (the objectui#11136 harness). The navigation was `[{ id: 'nav_home', type: 'page', label: { en: 'Home', 'zh-CN': '首页' }, pageName: 'home' }]` plus a plain Landing page. React logged `Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {en, zh-CN})`, and neither nav button rendered: the pillar's rail is gone. In the control leg, the same harness with `label: 'Home'` logged 0 errors and the rail rendered `Home`. The run was in happy-dom, not a browser.
- **Spec-valid input.** `NavigationItemSchema` accepts the map (`safeParse` true).
- **Confirmed at source.** PR objectui#11157's contract review (`5901615510`, ③ out-of-scope (a)) confirmed both sites at its head `575bbb6e6`: real, pre-existing, and untouched by that PR.

Reader: triage first (grade and route), then the seat that dispatches it. Filed by `domain:ui` seat 2 (`session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`) at the ACCEPT of PR objectui#11157 (objectui#11148), from the dev report's `out_of_scope_findings[0]` (`5901455875`). ⛔ Not graded here. Severity as measured: a crash of the pillar's rail, not a mis-read.

## The sites (read at objectui `origin/main` `a782fa732`)

- **`NavTree`** in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` renders the nav node's `label` raw, three times:
  - the group heading, `{node.label}` beside the `Folder` icon;
  - the entry button's text, `{node.label || surface?.name}`;
  - the button's `title` attribute (`… : node.label`).
- **`resolveSurface`** in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/navSurface.ts` reads `const label = String(node.label ?? '')` into `Surface.label`, which the canvas title prints as `[object Object]`. The function takes no locale.

## Family

This is the same family as objectui#11100 (the app preview), objectui#11128 (the app designer's canvas) and objectui#11148 (the nav-item inspector): a nav item's `I18nLabel` read as a string in the Studio. The canvas and the inspector now resolve through one internal module, `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/navItemLabel.ts` (`navItemLabelText(label, locale)`, landing with PR objectui#11157), in the designer locale from `useMetadataLocale()`.

## Direction (for triage, not a ruling)

- `NavTree` resolves each node's label through that one helper, in the designer locale, for the heading, the entry text and the `title` attribute.
- `resolveSurface` carries the resolved text rather than a `String()` of the map. Either it takes a locale, or its callers hand it the resolved label. Three callers read it at `a782fa732`: `NavTree`; the first-leaf auto-open when the app draft loads; and `findSurfaceInTree` in `navSurface.ts`, which backs the `?surface=` deep-link restore. The `?surface=` restore is a different parameter from objectui#11153's `?sel=nav:ID`, but it sits in the same load path.
- Pins:
  - a map-labelled nav item renders its en text under en and its zh text under zh, in the rail and in the canvas title, with no React error;
  - a plain-string label renders as today (the control).

Serial: `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` is objectui#11148's file (PR objectui#11157, merging) and objectui#11153's. This card and objectui#11153 edit the same component's load path, so they run one after the other, not in parallel.

## Dedupe

The 1000 most recently updated objectui issues and PRs, open and closed (down to #10369), were grepped:
- `resolveSurface` and `navSurface`: 1 hit each, PR objectui#11157 (the source).
- `NavTree`: 1 hit, objectui#11153 (the deep link, a different defect in the same component).
- `not valid as a React child`: 16 hits, all other components (the `plugin-form` / `ComponentPropsMap` families).
- `Surface.label`: 0 hits.

objectui#11100 covered `AppPreview`, not the Interfaces rail, and is closed. No card covers this.
